messages:
Olivia (support): Hey team — customer running Redwood Private in their VPC. Installer fails mid-way: pip wheels time out and the model shard download fails. They want a minimal outbound allowlist we can share. Can someone assemble hosts/ports and callouts?

deploy-bot: [installer] ERROR: curl https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/... -> SSL: certificate verify failed (60)
installer: download model shard https://model-shard-us-west-2.s3.amazonaws.com/abc.part -> connection reset after 30s

Matt (onprem): Ok — first Qs: are they doing TLS intercept / proxy with cert rewrap? That often breaks pip and S3 presigned URLs. Also do they expect to whitelist IPs or hostnames?

Olivia (support): Customer says they have a corporate proxy doing MITM for TLS inspection. They asked for IPs because firewall only allows IP ranges.

Priya (infra): Short answer: we recommend allowlisting hostnames/SNI, not static IPs — many Redwood deps are S3/CloudFront or third-party CDNs with dynamic IPs. If they must use IPs, call out AWS prefix list for the region (link it).

Alex (eng): Here is a trimmed recommended allowlist (outbound TCP 443 unless noted):
```
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- wheelhouse caches (if using internal cache) e.g., artifactory.company.com
- github.com, codeload.github.com
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- model-shard-*.s3.amazonaws.com (region specific)
- *.cloudfront.net
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai (OAuth token endpoints)
- sts.amazonaws.com, iam.amazonaws.com
- kms.<region>.amazonaws.com (if using AWS KMS)
- ocsp.* (OCSP responders, port 80 HTTP for OCSP requests)
- crl.* (CRL distribution points, port 80)
```

Matt (onprem): Add notes:
- Ports: 443 outbound for HTTPS; some OCSP/CRL checks use HTTP (port 80) — allow outbound 80 to OCSP/CRL hosts.
- SNI: proxy must preserve SNI host header and NOT substitute certs for these endpoints, otherwise presigned S3 URLs and signature checks fail.
- Timeouts: model shard downloads are large — ensure proxy/firewall idle timeouts >= 300s and allow chunked transfer.

Olivia (support): Customer's curl output (sanitized):
```
* Connected to files.pythonhosted.org (10.20.30.40) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

Priya (infra): That looks like a cert chain/trust issue caused by TLS interception. Two mitigation paths:
- Preferable: configure proxy to bypass (no interception) for the hosts above.
- If bypass not possible: ensure the proxy's signing CA is trusted by the installer environment (OS trust store + containers). Note: even if CA is trusted, presigned S3 URLs sometimes validate host certs strictly — bypass is better.

Alex (eng): For model registry & shard specifics:
- model-registry.redwood.ai: token exchange and metadata calls (short TLS sessions).
- Shards served from S3/CloudFront: presigned URLs with Host header & signature. Any TLS rewrap/break will invalidate signatures -> 403/403-like errors.
- Large shards: allow HEAD/GET to Content-Length large and increase reverse-proxy buffering limits.

Matt (onprem): If they insist on IP ranges, provide AWS published prefixes: https://ip-ranges.amazonaws.com/ip-ranges.json and CloudFront IP ranges. But warn that ranges change frequently. Recommend using AWS prefix-list (managed) if their firewall supports it.

Priya (infra): Telemetry/auth specifics:
- telemetry.redwood.ai: 443 outbound for metrics/traces. If telemetry is blocked, customer will see installer hang on "registering instance" events.
- auth.redwood.ai and token endpoints: 443 outbound; firewall must allow CONNECT to these hosts.
- If using a private KMS, ensure outbound to KMS endpoints and STS for the regions in use.

Alex (eng): Quick example firewall rule snippet customers can adapt (hostname-based allow):
```
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 TO *.pythonhosted.org
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 TO *.pypi.org
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 TO *.github.com
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 TO model-registry.redwood.ai
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 TO *.s3.amazonaws.com
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 TO *.cloudfront.net
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 TO telemetry.redwood.ai
ALLOW TCP OUT 443 TO auth.redwood.ai
ALLOW TCP OUT 80  TO ocsp.*
```

Olivia (support): Customer asked about OCSP specifically — do we have a short list of OCSP responders our clients hit?

Priya (infra): OCSP/CRL responders vary by CA. Common ones we see: ocsp.digicert.com, ocsp.globalsign.com, crl3.digicert.com. Tell the customer to allow outbound HTTP to OCSP/CRL hostnames or ensure proxy forwards OCSP requests unchanged.

Matt (onprem): Also callout for on-prem installers behind a pure SNI-pass-through proxy: they must allow CONNECT so the TLS handshake is end-to-end. If the proxy performs MITM, we will see SSL errors like Olivia pasted.

Olivia (support): I’ll pass the hostname list and the guidance about OCSP and KMS. One more ask from customer: they want a short checklist for their security team explaining why we need hostname/SNI bypass vs IP allowlist. Can someone draft 3 bullets?

Alex (eng): Draft bullets:
- Many Redwood dependencies are served from cloud CDNs (S3/CloudFront) with elastic IPs; IP ranges change and presigned URLs depend on TLS host validation — TLS interception breaks signatures.
- OCSP/CRL checks require intact TLS/HTTP access; interception or blocking causes cert validation failures for pip/curl and installer.
- If IP-only firewall is mandatory, use cloud provider managed prefix lists (AWS ip-ranges.json or AWS-managed prefix-list) and accept frequent updates; recommend exceptions for auth/telemetry endpoints.

Priya (infra): +1 and add: allowlist maintenance: schedule a weekly sync or automate via API to pull AWS ip-ranges.json if they must keep IP rules.

Olivia (support): Great — sent to customer. They applied rules for pypi, files.pythonhosted.org, telemetry.redwood.ai and disabled TLS intercept for those hosts. Will wait for their retest. :white_check_mark:

Matt (onprem): If they still see errors, ask them to run these checks and paste results:
```
curl -vI https://files.pythonhosted.org/
curl -vI https://model-registry.redwood.ai/healthz
python -c "import ssl, socket; s=ssl.create_default_context(); conn=s.wrap_socket(socket.socket(), server_hostname='files.pythonhosted.org'); conn.connect(('files.pythonhosted.org', 443)); print(conn.getpeercert())"
```

Olivia (support): Thanks all — I’ll follow up after the test. Keeping thread open until customer confirms. :eyes:
